title: Mini Auditing-Sabotage Bench: Can Cheap Open Models Detect Subtle ML-Code Sabotage?

original_idea.body:
# Mini Auditing-Sabotage Bench: Can Cheap Open Models Detect Subtle ML-Code Sabotage?

**Problem:** Auditing Sabotage Bench shows frontier auditors top out at AUROC 0.77 / 42% fix rate on detecting sabotaged ML codebases. It is unknown how far below this a cheap, open, locally-runnable auditor model falls, and which sabotage types (hyperparameter vs data vs eval-code) are hardest.

**Direction:** Reconstruct a small subset of sabotaged/clean ML-code snippet pairs in the style of the benchmark (modified hyperparameters, swapped data filters, tampered eval code). Prompt 1-2 open models to flag sabotage, score detection AUROC per sabotage category, and compare to the reported frontier numbers. Identify the category with the largest open-vs-frontier gap.

**Why it matters:** AI R&D sabotage by automated systems is a medium-horizon threat labs deprioritize. Establishing how detectable it is with only cheap, open auditors tells the external safety community whether decentralized monitoring is viable and where it fails. No training, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Auditing Sabotage Bench: A Benchmark for Detecting and Fixing Research Sabotage in ML Codebases (arXiv:2604.16286, Apr 2026; best AUROC 0.77, top-1 fix 42% by Gemini 3.1 Pro). CTRL-ALT-DECEIT: Sabotage Evaluations for Automated AI R&D (arXiv:2511.09904).
